data.narrative:
Anthro Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Jonathan Hes, David Mackanic, and Joe Papp that has raised $53.3M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine private peers and one public comparable (LNZA), though the private peer set—which includes Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with aligned valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised as a proxy baseline ($53M) and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $107M. This method is applicable where investor step-ups follow predictable patterns at frontier-tech stages, though it assumes execution risk and market conditions remain stable.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $91M to $123M, with a median point of $107M. This range reflects reasonable confidence intervals around the stage-progression anchor but relies on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight-fit peer comparables in Climate & Energy at the Series A stage, making it difficult to benchmark against similar-stage capital deployments or implied revenue multiples. Investor should validate this range against forward metrics (capital efficiency, burn rate, unit economics) and update if material peer data emerges.
